rules.law_name: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance
rules.citation: Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal Code
rules.effective_date_basis: The Ordinance goes into effect June 24, 2023.
rules.title: San Diego just-cause eviction and relocation protections
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a covered residential tenancy only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes, with required notices and cure opportunities for curable lease violations. For no-fault terminations, tenants are entitled to relocation assistance of two months’ actual rent, or three months’ actual rent if elderly or disabled, and may have a right to an offer to re-rent if the unit is offered again within five years.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance of 2 months' actual rent, or 3 months' actual rent for elderly or disabled tenants

coverage.small_owner_exception: A residential rental unit, including a mobilehome, that is alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with at least one corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and tenants receive written notice of the exemption.
coverage.other_unresolvable: The ordinance applies only to a tenancy, defined as the lawful right to continuously use or occupy a residential rental property for more than 30 days, and excludes fixed-term leases of three months or less; transient/tourist hotels; occupancies of 30 days or less; certain affordable housing or subsidy-restricted housing; mobilehomes subject to the MRL; specified nonprofit, hospital, religious, extended-care, elderly-care, transitional-housing, and higher-education dormitory accommodations; units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains a principal residence there; and certain owner-occupied single-family, mobilehome, and duplex arrangements.
coverage.summary: Applies to covered San Diego residential tenancies over 30 days, including rented dwellings in mobilehome parks, subject to numerous exemptions for short-term, institutional, affordable, owner-occupied, separately alienable, and newer housing.

rules.exemptions: Not subject to the Ordinance: transient and tourist hotel tenants; occupancies by concession, permit, right of access, license, or other agreement for 30 consecutive days or less; deed- or government-restricted affordable housing, except the exclusion does not apply to tenants with Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers; mobilehomes subject to the MRL; specified nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elderly care, nonprofit transitional housing, and school-owned dormitory housing; units where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains a principal residence there; single-family owner-occupied residences including mobilehomes where the owner rents no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes meeting stated conditions; separately alienable units meeting stated ownership and notice conditions; and housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless the dwelling is a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: A tenant may file an action, seek injunctive relief, equitable relief, money damages including punitive damages, and raise violations as an affirmative defense in unlawful detainer. An attempted or actual recovery of possession in violation of the ordinance can make the landlord liable for at least three times actual economic damages, and failure to provide relocation assistance can make the landlord liable for at least three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages; reasonable attorney’s fees and costs are available in non-unlawful-detainer civil actions.
rules.interaction: The document states the Ordinance requires just cause for termination consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2 and that notices also reference California Civil Code section 1947.12 rent-increase limits.
